To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
European origin does not influence the provision of health‐ care and prognosis of HIV patients in Europe; however non‐European origin does.
the origin of patients with HIV infection is associated with differences in access to care and survival.
European origin is associated with higher CD4 count, higher CD4/CD8 ratio, higher viral load and lower mortality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: Does European or non-European origin influence health care for HIV patients in the Netherlands?
the following questions: Does the origin of the patient influence the provision of health‐ care and survival among HIV infected patients in Europe?
the following questions: Does the European or non‐EUROPEAN origin of HIV patients influence their access to health care and their prognosis?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the prognosis of HIV patients is better in Europe than in North America and that the prognosis for patients from non‐European origin is worse than for patients from European origin.
European and non‐European patients with HIV infection are equally well treated, and that survival is not affected by origin.
there are no significant differences between European and non‐European patients with regard to the quality of care and survival.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the European patients had a better access to health‐care, a better survival, and a higher CD4 count at start of HAART than the non‐European patients.
the European or non‐ European origin of patients with HIV does not seem to influence health care and survival in Europe.
the European origin does not have any impact on health care or prognosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have a better understanding of the role of the immune system and its role in the development and treatment of cancer.
the HIV epidemic is a global problem and that it is important to understand how HIV affects patients in other countries and continents.
there is a clear association between the country of origin of HIV patients and the quality of their health care.
